evals.prompt: Run this week's pulse. Here are the champion notes and the survey export (agents n=96, team leaders n=12, payroll n=3).
evals.expected_output: Reports themes by group with signal counts and sources, compares survey % agree with the previous wave, combines or drops the payroll group (below minimum size), states coverage gaps, and proposes resistance-log rows; writes nothing until the user says yes.
assertions: Does not report results for the group with 3 responses on its own
Every theme cites a source type and a count of signals
Survey figures are shown with the number of responses
States which sources were and were not read
Proposes resistance-log rows and waits for approval before writing
Does not quote or name any individual

evals.prompt: We're six weeks out from go-live. Write the pulse survey questions for the contact centre.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the six core questions plus one or two Manage-phase questions and at most one open question from pulse-questions.md, a single group question, a short note on how answers are used, and a suggested cadence; does not send or publish anything.
assertions: Includes the six core questions with their wording unchanged in meaning
Adds no more than two phase questions and no more than one open question
Asks for the group only, never a name or employee ID
Uses one agreement scale for every closed question
Does not claim the survey has been sent or scheduled

evals.prompt: Agree on 'I understand why' went from 70% to 74% this wave in finance (n=15). Is understanding improving?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a 4-point change on 15 responses is not a clear trend under the plugin's rule and reports it as no clear change.
assertions: Reports the movement as no clear change rather than an improvement
Refers to the response count when explaining why
